skill.name: remove-git-worktree
skill.description: Removes a Git worktree for a named branch and deletes the matching local branch after cleanup.
skill.summary: Clean up a Git worktree and its local branch from a repository.
skill.author: AKABANAKK

security_audit.summary: Most command-execution findings are expected for a Git cleanup script and are false positives because commands are hardcoded and quoted. The parent-relative worktree path and later delete operations are real risks because the skill can remove a sibling worktree directory and force-delete a local branch without confirmation. No evidence found for prompt injection or network behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve and validate the canonical path, require it to stay inside the expected worktrees directory, and reject unexpected names before removal.
Show the resolved worktree path and branch name, then require explicit user confirmation before removing the worktree or deleting the branch.
Validate input with Git branch-name checks and reject values that do not match an existing local branch.

finding_verdicts.reason: The command substitution uses hardcoded echo and tr commands with the branch name quoted. It only converts slashes to hyphens and does not evaluate user input as shell syntax.
The git rev-parse command is hardcoded and only discovers the repository root. No user-controlled command or argument is injected into this substitution.
The basename command is hardcoded and receives the quoted repository path from Git. This is normal path extraction, not shell execution from untrusted input.
The shebang declares that the helper script runs with Bash. It is not by itself a hidden command-execution behavior or injection vector.
The script builds a parent-relative path outside the repository root and later removes that worktree path. This is intended cleanup behavior, but it is still a real filesystem deletion risk.
The flagged text is the opening fence of a Markdown command example. It is not Ruby backtick execution and does not execute by itself.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Cleanup Runs Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The script removes the computed worktree and then force-deletes a matching local branch when it exists. It does not ask for confirmation before the destructive operations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file directly invokes git worktree remove and git branch -D on the selected branch context. The behavior is intended by the skill but can delete local work.

high_findings.title: Path traversal sequence
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script builds a parent-relative path outside the repository root and later removes that worktree path. This is intended cleanup behavior, but it is still a real filesystem deletion risk.

content.value_statement: Abandoned Git worktrees can leave stale files and local branches behind. This skill runs a focused cleanup script for a named branch.
actual_capabilities: Shows the command for removing a worktree by branch name.
Converts branch slashes to hyphens for the expected worktree folder name.
Finds the current repository root with Git.
Removes the matching worktree with Git worktree commands.
Deletes the matching local branch when it exists.
limitations: Assumes worktrees live in a sibling directory named after the repository.
Does not ask for confirmation before removing the worktree.
Does not check for uncommitted changes before cleanup.
Does not delete remote branches or remote tracking references.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Completed Feature Work
use_cases.description: Remove a feature worktree and its local branch after merge work is finished.

use_cases.title: Recover From Accidental Worktree Creation
use_cases.description: Delete a mistakenly created worktree that follows the repository worktree naming convention.

use_cases.title: Keep Local Repositories Tidy
use_cases.description: Standardize cleanup of old local worktrees during repository maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Remove One Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the remove-git-worktree skill to remove the worktree for branch feature/new-login.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner cleanup for one known branch.

prompt_templates.title: Clean After Merge
prompt_templates.prompt: After confirming branch feature/cart-checkout is merged, remove its local worktree and matching local branch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Routine cleanup after a completed pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Path Before Removal
prompt_templates.prompt: For branch bugfix/header-layout, show the resolved worktree path first. Continue only if it matches the expected sibling worktrees directory.
prompt_templates.scenario: Safer cleanup when the repository layout matters.

prompt_templates.title: Review Cleanup Risk
prompt_templates.prompt: Before removing branch experiment/payment-flow, check whether local work may be lost and explain the cleanup impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before destructive local cleanup.

output_examples.output: The feature/new-login worktree was removed from the expected sibling worktrees directory. The matching local branch was also deleted.
The cleanup completed for bugfix/header-layout. The local worktree and local branch are no longer present.

output_examples.input: Verify the path before removing experiment/payment-flow.
output_examples.output: The resolved path matched the expected worktrees directory. Cleanup can continue after user confirmation.

best_practices: Run the skill from the correct Git repository.
Confirm the branch name and resolved worktree path before cleanup.
Commit, stash, or back up local changes before removing a worktree.
anti_patterns: Do not run cleanup with a guessed or partial branch name.
Do not use this skill on worktrees that may contain unsaved work.
Do not expect this skill to remove remote branches.

faq.question: What does this skill remove?
faq.answer: It removes a local Git worktree for a named branch and deletes the matching local branch when present.

faq.question: Does it remove remote branches?
faq.answer: No. It only targets local worktrees and local branches.

faq.question: Where does it expect worktrees to exist?
faq.answer: It expects a sibling worktrees directory based on the current repository name.

faq.question: Does it protect uncommitted work?
faq.answer: No. Users should commit, stash, or back up local changes before running cleanup.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after a branch worktree is no longer needed and local cleanup is safe.
